plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of a vector broken into components. Three axes meet at a common origin, x pointing toward the lower left and out of the page, y running to the right, and z pointing straight up, each drawn as a thin line with an arrowhead and an italic label. A dashed rectangular box is built on the origin with its edges lying along the three axes. Three heavy blue arrows run outward along those axes and are labeled as the component vectors: A_x = A_x i-hat along the x-axis, A_y = A_y j-hat along the y-axis, and A_z = A_z k-hat along the z-axis, with each label written alongside its arrow. A single red arrow starts at the origin, cuts diagonally through the interior of the box, and ends at the far corner where the dashed faces meet; it is labeled A = A_x + A_y + A_z, every symbol carrying an overhead vector arrow. Drawing the blue arrows as three edges of the box and the red arrow as its body diagonal lets the reader watch the three components add head to tail to rebuild the whole vector. The same box supports the two nested right triangles from which the magnitude of a three-dimensional vector is obtained.

elements: x-axis extending forward-left, with arrowhead and 'x' label
y-axis extending right, with arrowhead and 'y' label
z-axis extending up, with arrowhead and 'z' label
red resultant vector arrow starting at the origin and ending at (A_x, A_y, A_z)
three blue component vector arrows (A_x, A_y, A_z)
dashed rectangular bounding box with corners at the origin and (A_x, A_y, A_z), outlining the 3D space
label for the red vector: A = A_x + A_y + A_z (with vector arrows over variables)
labels for the blue vectors: A_x = A_x i-hat, A_y = A_y j-hat, A_z = A_z k-hat

interactions.teaches: The spatial nature of the 3D vector, allowing the learner to view the resultant and components from any angle.

interactions.label: A_x
interactions.teaches: Changing the x-component stretches the bounding box along the x-axis and alters the resultant vector's direction and magnitude.

interactions.label: A_y
interactions.teaches: Changing the y-component stretches the bounding box along the y-axis and alters the resultant vector's direction and magnitude.

interactions.label: A_z
interactions.teaches: Changing the z-component stretches the bounding box vertically and alters the resultant vector's direction and magnitude.

interactions.label: Vector Construction
interactions.teaches: Shows that placing the component vectors head-to-tail reaches the exact same final point in space as the simultaneous diagonal resultant.

demo_steps.title: 1D: X-axis only
demo_steps.narration: When A_y and A_z are zero, the vector lies entirely along the x-axis.

demo_steps.title: 2D: XY-plane
demo_steps.narration: Adding a y-component moves the vector into the xy-plane. It is now a 2D planar vector.

demo_steps.title: 3D: Full XYZ
demo_steps.narration: Adding a z-component lifts the vector into full 3D space, forming the diagonal of the bounding box.

demo_steps.title: Head-to-tail Addition
demo_steps.narration: By arranging the three components head-to-tail, they trace a path along the edges of the box that perfectly matches the diagonal resultant.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axes span from origin to 6 units in +x, +y, +z. The resultant vector is a red arrow (#cc2200) from (0,0,0) to (ax, ay, az). Component arrows are heavy blue (#1a66cc). The dashed box uses thin gray lines outlining the parallelepiped (width ax, depth ay, height az). In 'Simultaneous' mode, blue arrows start at the origin and run along the axes. In 'Head-to-tail' mode, Ax runs from (0,0,0) to (ax,0,0); Ay runs from (ax,0,0) to (ax,ay,0); Az runs from (ax,ay,0) to (ax,ay,az).
interactionPlan.notes: Reactively update vector endpoints, dashed box dimensions, and label positions when sliders change. If a component is 0, hide its arrow and label to avoid visual artifacts. Animate the transition between Simultaneous and Head-to-tail modes if possible, translating the Ay and Az arrows to their new positions.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Preset vector cases: choose x-only, xy-plane, or full xyz components and the component arrows plus resultant update, showing when a vector is axis-aligned, planar, or genuinely spatial.
- Slider for component values A_x, A_y, and A_z: learner adjusts each component with separate controls; the box dimensions, blue edge arrows, and red resultant update together; the relationship between components and resultant magnitude or direction becomes visible.
- Toggle between simultaneous components and head-to-tail build: learner switches the construction mode; the blue arrows either sit on the box edges or animate sequentially from one arrowhead to the next before ending at the red vector tip; the equivalence between component decomposition and vector addition becomes clear.

authoredContext:
In three-dimensional space, vector A→ has three vector components: the x-component A→x=Axi^, which is the part of vector A→ along the x-axis; the y-component A→y=Ayj^, which is the part of A→ along the y-axis; and the z-component A→z=Azk^, which is the part of the vector along the z-axis. A vector in three-dimensional space is the vector sum of its three vector components (the figure):

This expression for the vector magnitude comes from applying the Pythagorean theorem twice. As seen in the figure, the diagonal in the xy-plane has length Ax2+Ay2 and its square adds to the square Az2 to give A2. Note that when the z-component is zero, the vector lies entirely in the xy-plane and its description is reduced to two dimensions.

A vector in three-dimensional space is the vector sum of its three vector components.

Vector A in the x y z coordinate system extends from the origin. Vector A equals the sum of vectors A sub x, A sub y and A sub z. Vector A sub x is the x component along the x axis and has length A sub x I hat. Vector A sub y is the y component along the y axis and has length A sub y j hat. Vector A sub z is the z component along the z axis and has length A sub x k hat. The components form the sides of a rectangular box with sides length A sub x, A sub y, and A sub z.

Three axes meet at a common origin, x pointing toward the lower left and out of the page, y running to the right, and z pointing straight up, each drawn as a thin line with an arrowhead and an italic label. A dashed rectangular box is built on the origin with its edges lying along the three axes. Three heavy blue arrows run outward along those axes and are labeled as the component vectors: A_x = A_x i-hat along the x-axis, A_y = A_y j-hat along the y-axis, and A_z = A_z k-hat along the z-axis, with each label written alongside its arrow. A single red arrow starts at the origin, cuts diagonally through the interior of the box, and ends at the far corner where the dashed faces meet; it is labeled A = A_x + A_y + A_z, every symbol carrying an overhead vector arrow. Drawing the blue arrows as three edges of the box and the red arrow as its body diagonal lets the reader watch the three components add head to tail to rebuild the whole vector. The same box supports the two nested right triangles from which the magnitude of a three-dimensional vector is obtained.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Preset vector cases: choose x-only, xy-plane, or full xyz components and the component arrows plus resultant update, showing when a vector is axis-aligned, planar, or genuinely spatial.
- Slider for component values A_x, A_y, and A_z: learner adjusts each component with separate controls; the box dimensions, blue edge arrows, and red resultant update together; the relationship between components and resultant magnitude or direction becomes visible.
- Toggle between simultaneous components and head-to-tail build: learner switches the construction mode; the blue arrows either sit on the box edges or animate sequentially from one arrowhead to the next before ending at the red vector tip; the equivalence between component decomposition and vector addition becomes clear.
